findings.resolution: Added `assertWellFormedUtf16` in packages/core/src/canonical.ts that rejects every string containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate with the new `E_ILL_FORMED_STRING` code, invoked from both `encodeValue`'s string branch and `encodeObject`'s per-key path before descriptor lookup. Under this rule the input to `TextEncoder.encode` is always well-formed, UTF-8 encoding is injective, and the `"\uD800"`/`"�"` object-key collision is impossible. ADR-009 §2/§3/§5/§7.2 updated: strings must be well-formed UTF-16, the rejection table adds `E_ILL_FORMED_STRING`, §5 now proves ties cannot occur for admitted keys, and §7.2 documents UTF-8 injectivity. Added tests/canonical/hostile-string.test.mjs with 14 cases covering lone high/low surrogates, mid-string unpaired surrogates, unpaired-at-end, adjacent high surrogates, valid surrogate pair (emoji) acceptance, well-formed U+FFFD acceptance, lone-surrogate rejection at object keys and nested-Set elements, an opposite-construction-order INV-22 rejection proof for the exact `"\uD800"`/`"�"` pair, and a golden vector for `{ '�': 1, 'a': 2 }` demonstrating UTF-8 byte-order sorting on the well-formed side.

Captured every previously-runtime-resolved mutable intrinsic at module init in packages/core/src/canonical.ts: `capturedArrayPrototypePush`, `capturedArrayPrototypeSort`, `capturedUint8Array` (constructor), `capturedUint8ArrayPrototypeSet`, `capturedStringPrototypeCharCodeAt`, `capturedStringPrototypeCharAt`. Every `new Uint8Array(...)`, `Uint8Array.of(...)`, `.push(...)`, `.sort(...)`, `.set(...)` on the emitted buffer, and every `str.charCodeAt(...)`/`str.charAt(...)` inside the encoder now goes through the captured reference via `capturedReflectApply` (helpers `pushInto`, `sortWith`, `charCodeAt`, `charAt`, `bytesFromCodes`, `concatChunks`). Removed the internal `new Set<string>()` used for object-key deduplication (ECMA-262 `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` already guarantees a duplicate-free list; the `E_DUPLICATE_KEY` code was dead and has been removed from the union). Converted every internal `for..of` to indexed `for (let i = 0; i < .length; i += 1)` loops so `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` / `TypedArray.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` cannot influence traversal. ADR-009 §6 now lists the exhaustive captured-intrinsic set (including the newly captured entries), §6 states the encoder no longer uses `for..of` on caller-tamperable containers, and §6 documents that `globalThis.Set` never participates in encoder execution paths. tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs adds 11 new post-import monkey-patch tests using a delegating-hostile pattern that counts invocations while forwarding to the original (so node:test's own use of the intrinsic still works). Each new test proves both `bytesEqual(before, after)` and a zero-invocation counter for `Array.prototype.push`, `Array.prototype.sort`, `Uint8Array.prototype.set`, `globalThis.Uint8Array`, `Uint8Array.of`, `globalThis.Set`, `String.prototype.charCodeAt` (on integers and on ill-formed-string rejection), and `String.prototype.charAt`.

Ran the complete CI-equivalent validation gate after applying the fixes. `npm run compile` (strict typecheck under tsconfig.base.json with `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `useUnknownInCatchVariables`, and 15 project references) exits 0 with no output. `npm run lint` (eslint --max-warnings=0 across the monorepo) exits 0 with no output. `npm run boundary` (tools/boundary/check.mjs) prints `dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against §14.5.` and exits 0. `npm test` (node --test over tests/config, tests/lint, tests/boundary, tests/canonical) reports `# tests 157 # pass 157 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0` — up from 134 pre-change, reflecting the 14 new hostile-string cases and 11 additional monkey-patch cases. Command lines and PASS results captured in `validation` below.

notes_for_reviewer: REVIEW-001 fix chose the deterministic-rejection path recommended by the review (over an injective WTF-8-style encoding), matching the ADR-009 principle that violations are errors, not silent normalisations. A future admitted-state surface that needs arbitrary UTF-16 keys can revisit this via an ADR revision that bumps the encoding version.

REVIEW-002 fix eliminated the internal duplicate-key `Set` entirely rather than capturing the `Set` constructor. ECMA-262 `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` guarantees a duplicate-free list of own string keys, so the check was dead code. As a side effect, `globalThis.Set` no longer participates in any encoder execution path, and the removed `E_DUPLICATE_KEY` code has been dropped from `CanonicalEncoderErrorCode` (no consumer exists yet).

REVIEW-002 fix also converted every internal `for..of` traversal to an indexed `for (let i = 0; i < .length; i += 1)` loop so `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` and `TypedArray.prototype[Symbol.iterator]` cannot influence encoder behaviour. This is documented in ADR-009 §6.

The new monkey-patch tests use a delegating-hostile pattern (`withDelegatingPatch` in tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs) that forwards to the original method while counting invocations. This is required because non-delegating no-op hostiles break node:test's internal use of the same prototype methods (e.g. Uint8Array.prototype.set is used by the v8 test reporter). The delegating pattern still proves the encoder-side property: the counter stays at zero exactly when the encoder ignores the patched global. The tests also handle inherited-vs-own descriptor semantics correctly, e.g. Uint8Array.prototype.set is inherited from %TypedArray%.prototype.set.

The v1 grammar and encoding version are unchanged; well-formed byte output for previously admitted inputs is byte-identical to the prior candidate. All 134 originally-accepted tests continue to pass, and the 23 additional tests exercise only the new rejection surface and the newly captured intrinsics.
payload.summary: Resolved all three review findings. (1) Added `E_ILL_FORMED_STRING` rejection for unpaired UTF-16 surrogates and updated ADR-009 so admitted strings are well-formed UTF-16, restoring UTF-8 injectivity and closing the `"\uD800"`/`"�"` object-key collision that violated INV-22. (2) Captured every remaining mutable operation used by the encoder — `Array.prototype.push`/`sort`, `Uint8Array` constructor, `Uint8Array.prototype.set`, `String.prototype.charCodeAt`/`charAt` — eliminated `Uint8Array.of`, removed the internal duplicate-key `Set` (redundant with ECMA-262 `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]`), converted every internal `for..of` to indexed loops, and updated the ADR's exhaustive captured-intrinsic list to match. (3) Ran and passed `npm run compile`, `npm run lint`, `npm run boundary`, and `npm test` (157 tests, up from 134) — evidence attached in `validation`.

eslint --max-warnings=0 . reports no errors or warnings across the monorepo.
tools/boundary/check.mjs prints 'dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against §14.5.' and exits 0.

node --test over tests/config, tests/lint, tests/boundary, tests/canonical reports 157/157 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 0 todo — includes 14 new hostile-string cases (lone surrogates, mid-string surrogates, unpaired-at-end, adjacent high surrogates, valid emoji, well-formed U+FFFD, key/nested/Set-element paths, opposite-construction-order INV-22 collision rejection, well-formed byte-order golden) and 11 new post-import monkey-patch cases (Array.prototype.push/sort, Uint8Array.prototype.set, globalThis.Uint8Array, Uint8Array.of, globalThis.Set, String.prototype.charCodeAt on integers, String.prototype.charAt, String.prototype.charCodeAt on ill-formed-string rejection).
All 14 new UTF-16 well-formedness / INV-22 collision tests pass, including the direct opposite-construction-order rejection proof for objects containing keys '\uD800' and '�'.

All 35 monkey-patch tests pass (24 pre-existing + 11 new). Every new delegating-hostile test asserts calls == 0 for the encoder, proving the captured intrinsic bypasses every post-import replacement of Array.prototype.push/sort, Uint8Array.prototype.set, globalThis.Uint8Array, Uint8Array.of, globalThis.Set, and String.prototype.charCodeAt/charAt.
